record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For each dimension m, let α_m be the smallest constant such that every quadratic stochastic operator V on S^{m-1} satisfying P_{ij,k} > α_m for all heredity coefficients is regular. The paper states that if P_{ij,k} > 1/(2m), then V is regular, and it gives the exact value of α_2. Determine the exact value of α_m for every m >= 3.

evidence.quote: In [17] the authors consider an arbitrary QSO V : S m−1 → S m−1 with matrix P = (Pij,k ) and studied the problem of finding the smallest αm such that the condition Pij,k > αm implies the regularity of V . Theorem 7. [17] 1) If Pij,k > 1/2m then V is regular. 2) α2 = 1/2 (3 − √7).
Problem 12. Find exact values of αm for any m ≥ 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m\ge 2$ and let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m:\ x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex of probability vectors.

A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ is a map of the form
$$ (Vx)_k \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m} P_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m, $$
where the heredity coefficients $\{P_{ij,k}\}$ satisfy
$$ P_{ij,k}=P_{ji,k}\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{m}P_{ij,k}=1\ \ \text{for all } i,j\in\{1,\dots,m\}. $$

The operator $V$ is called regular if for every initial point $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$ the iterates $x^{(n+1)}=V(x^{(n)})$ converge, as $n\to\infty$, to a limit which does not depend on $x^{(0)}$.

For each integer $m\ge 2$ define
$$ \alpha_m \;=\; \inf\Big\{\alpha\in[0,1]:\ \text{every QSO } V \text{ on } S^{m-1} \text{ with } P_{ij,k}>\alpha \text{ for all } i,j,k \text{ is regular}\Big\}. $$

It is known that $\alpha_m\le \tfrac{1}{2m}$ and that $\alpha_2=\tfrac{1}{2}(3-\sqrt{7})$.

Determine the exact value of $\alpha_m$ for every integer $m\ge 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for results determining the exact regularity threshold $\alpha_m$ on the simplex $S^{m-1}$ for $m\ge 3$ did not turn up a published exact formula. Subsequent surveys on quadratic stochastic operators continue to discuss regularity criteria but do not appear to report a closed-form value of $\alpha_m$ for general $m\ge 3$, so the status is best recorded as unknown/likely still open.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators and Their Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on QSOs discussing regularity but not providing a closed form for alpha_m for m>=3.
status_evidence.claim: No exact value of alpha_m for m>=3 is reported.

status_evidence.title: On Regularity of Diagonally Positive Quadratic Doubly Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies regularity for special classes of QSOs without resolving the general threshold problem.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses related regularity questions; does not establish alpha_m for m>=3.
